title: Constant cohomology of the affine line
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or an algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $\bar k$ be an algebraic closure. Use the affine line [def-sbc-affine-space] and ordinary adic constant-coefficient cohomology in the common finite-stage coefficient category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Then, for every $q\geq0$,
$$
H^q(\mathbf A^1_{\bar k},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\cong\begin{cases}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell,&q=0,\\0,&q>0.\end{cases}
$$
The degree-zero isomorphism is induced by constant sections.

proof.text: Put $K=\bar k$ and $X=\mathbf A^1_K=\operatorname{Spec}K[t]$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. The zero ideal of $K[t]$ is prime, since the leading coefficient of a product of nonzero polynomials is nonzero; it belongs to every nonempty basic open, so $X$ is nonempty and irreducible, hence connected. The polynomial dimension theorem [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-dimension-one] gives dimension one. The projection is smooth of relative dimension one by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Thus $X$ is a smooth affine connected curve. It is separated and of finite type (one polynomial generator), and $\ell^n$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}K$ for every $n\geq1$.

source.place: Opening assertion that the affine line is irreducible and connected; hypotheses for the affine-curve calculations.

proof.text: For every $n\geq1$, apply [sbc-thm-cohomological-dimension-of-an-affine-curve] to $X$ and $d=\ell^n$. It gives $H^0(X_{\mathrm{et}},\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z})\cong\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ via constant sections, and $H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z})=0$ for every $q>1$. In particular these groups are finite.

source.place: Finite-level degree zero and higher-degree vanishing.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-primitive-root], choose a primitive $\ell^n$-th root of unity over $K$ at each $n$. Its trivialization allows application of the Kummer short exact sequence in [thm-sc-affine-cohomology]. That statement gives the unit quotient, $H^1(X,\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z})$, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[\ell^n]$ as its three terms; it explicitly says the unit term vanishes for $X=\mathbf A^1$. The statement of [lem-pur-affine-punctured-line-algebra] gives $\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbf A^1_K)=0$. Both outside terms of the sequence are therefore zero, forcing $H^1(X,\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z})=0$. No compatibility between the choices of roots of unity is needed: this proves that the actual constant-sheaf groups vanish. Together with Step 2, every finite-level cohomology group in nonnegative degree is finite.

source.place: Kummer computation and the Picard vanishing for the affine line.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fd-qbar-cohomology-finite-level-comparison] to $X$. Step 1 verifies its geometric and characteristic hypotheses, and Steps 2 and 3 verify finiteness in every nonnegative degree at every level. For each $q\geq0$ it identifies the desired adic cohomology with $(\varprojlim_n H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z))\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For $q>0$ all factors in that inverse limit are zero, so the inverse limit and its tensor product are zero.

source.place: Passage from compatible finite coefficients to adic algebraically closed coefficients, including its finiteness hypothesis.

proof.text: For $q=0$, the isomorphisms in Step 2 commute with the quotient transitions: reducing the constant section $a$ gives the constant section $a\bmod\ell^n$. Consequently their inverse limit is $\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. By [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property], applied to the ring of compatible tuples with its residue projections, the canonical map $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ is an isomorphism: the unique lift of the projections is its inverse, since the two composites agree on every residue projection. The tensor product of this free rank-one $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module with $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, via $z\otimes a\mapsto za$ with inverse $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. The constant-section compatibility in [lem-fd-qbar-cohomology-finite-level-comparison] makes this precisely the asserted degree-zero identification.

source.place: Constant-section degree-zero identification after the inverse limit and scalar extension.

blueprint_update.statement:
For $k$ finite or algebraically closed, with cohomology of the pro-étale
site and the coefficient sheaf $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell}=p^*\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$ of [def-sf-setting],

$$
H^q(\mathbf A^1_{\bar k},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)=\begin{cases}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell,&q=0,\\0,&q>0.\end{cases}
$$

proof.text:
*Torsion coefficients.* For every $n\ge1$, $H^q(X,\mathbf Z/\ell^n)$ is
$\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ for $q=0$, since $X$ is connected, and $0$ for $q>0$: the
vanishing for $q>1$ is the cohomological dimension of an affine curve of
[sbc-thm-cohomological-dimension-of-an-affine-curve], and
$H^1(X,\mathbf Z/\ell^n)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(X)[\ell^n]=0$ by
[thm-sc-affine-cohomology], the Picard group being trivial by
[lem-sc-pic-affine] (the compactification is $\mathbf P^1$ of genus $0$,
whose Jacobian is trivial, so the quotient of [lem-sc-pic-affine] is
$\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbf A^1)=0$). These are étale cohomology groups of
torsion sheaves, equal to the pro-étale ones.

*Integral coefficients.* By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x],
$\mathbf Z_{\ell,X}\simeq\varprojlim_n(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_X$, a limit of
classical sheaves with epimorphic transition maps, so
[sk-prop-pe-continuous-cohomology] gives exact sequences
$$
0\to\varprojlim\nolimits^1_nH^{q-1}(X,\mathbf Z/\ell^n)\to H^q(X,\mathbf Z_{\ell})
\to\varprojlim_nH^q(X,\mathbf Z/\ell^n)\to0 .
$$
The groups $H^{q-1}(X,\mathbf Z/\ell^n)$ are finite, so the $\varprojlim^1$
term vanishes, and $H^0(X,\mathbf Z_\ell)=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $H^q(X,\mathbf Z_\ell)=0$
for $q>0$. Thus $Ra_*\mathbf Z_{\ell,X}\simeq\mathbf Z_\ell$ in degree $0$.

*Coefficients $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.* The composite
$\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathbf Q_\ell\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is a coefficient
map of [sk-prop-scalar-six], so the coefficient comparison for $Ra_*$ gives
$Ra_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\simeq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z_\ell}Ra_*\mathbf Z_{\ell,X}
\simeq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ in degree $0$. Hence
$H^0(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and
$H^q(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)=0$ for $q>0$.
